paper.title: Building stock modelling for circularity: Insights from a Danish component-level model
paper.code_data_availability: Data availability statement: "Data will be made available on request." Supplementary information lists open-source code for the iBuildGreen model (https://github.com/NFrancart/iBuildGreen) and the macro-component catalogue. …

registers.name_in_paper: the national registry of buildings and housing (BBR)
registers.role: sample frame and all building-level inputs: building use, year of construction, footprint, gross floor area, number of floors, roof material and facade material
variables_mentioned: year of last renovation (named as available but not yet used)
area of integrated parking (named as available but not yet used)
presence of asbestos (named as available but not yet used)

registers.name_in_paper: LCAbyg (Danish building LCA tool) generic products and emission factors
registers.role: background environmental data: emission factors for each generic construction product, used for the embodied carbon replacement cost (EN 15804 modules A1-A3 and C3-C4)
variables_mentioned: emission factors (industry-branch EPDs or the German generic environmental database Oekobau)

registers.role: modelling input: typical wall, roof, slab, foundation and roof-cover solutions by period of use, with typical product amounts per m2 of component; compiled from Engelmark (2013) and design handbooks (Bonnesen, 1971; Nissen, 1984) and supplied as supplementary information
variables_mentioned: product amounts per m2 of wall/roof/slab
minimum and maximum viable roof pitch

registers.name_in_paper: dimensioning functions for inner walls from Mailhac (2019)
registers.role: modelling input: functions linking the surface of inner walls to floor area, extrapolated from French studies

linkages: Each BBR building is linked to a macro-component type for each building part through mapping tables in a PostgreSQL database (e.g. a 'building to roof' table), and each macro-component to its sub-components and products
Each product in the macro-component catalogue is mapped to a corresponding generic product in the Danish LCA tool LCAbyg, which supplies the emission factors
Model output is aggregated into Lanau & Liu's (2020) building-archetype categories (building type x construction period) to enable comparison with their material intensity coefficients

sample.universe: All buildings in the Danish national building registry (BBR); results are reported for the municipalities of Odense and Copenhagen, with national stock composition quoted for comparison
sample.unit_of_observation: building (results aggregated to material type x building element and to municipality)
selection_rules: Import BBR and remove entries missing key parameters (year of construction, roof material, facade material)
Remove entries with negative values for floor area or number of floors
Remove outliers that clearly represent data-entry mistakes (e.g. number of floors equal to the footprint or the floor area, or higher than the number of floors of the tallest skyscraper in Denmark)
Remove buildings with a footprint and floor area under 10 m2 (about 5 % of buildings in the database)
Where the footprint (or the floor area) was incorrectly entered, approximate the missing value from the number of floors and the floor area (or respectively the footprint)
Net effect: pre-processing removed close to 16 % of database entries, corresponding to 12 % of the reported gross floor area

construction_notes: Macro-component assignment: possible solutions are first narrowed by the BBR facade/roof cover material, then filtered by the year of construction; if several solutions fit, one is selected at random, and if none fits a random solution is selected

Building height is estimated from the number of floors and a standard floor-height value; roof pitch from the roof cover material; the perimeter from the footprint and a space-efficiency factor correcting for non-rectangular footprints
Internal-wall dimensioning functions are extrapolated from French studies (Mailhac, 2019); no Danish equivalents exist
Foundations and ground-floor slabs are dimensioned as generic material amounts per m2 of building footprint

Embodied carbon replacement cost covers EN 15804 modules A1-A3 (production) and C3-C4 (end-of-life treatment and disposal), with present-day emission factors and no evolution of emission factors over time
Wood products follow LCAbyg's '-1/+1' biogenic carbon convention: carbon counted as a sink in A1-A3 and released in C3
Basements, stairs and balconies are not modelled separately, and interdependences between components are not implemented
Non-residential buildings are largely not modelled separately except for inner walls, which consider building type
The model is implemented as a PostgreSQL relational database with a Python logic layer

The exclusion of close to 16 % of entries (12 % of gross floor area) means city-level material content is, in the authors' words, probably underestimated, while estimates of typical material content per building type improve

identification.source_of_variation: None: no exogenous variation is used. The quantity is a deterministic bottom-up accounting estimate (or a direct tabulation) built from the administrative BBR building registry.

key_assumptions.assumption: Each building's macro-components (external and internal walls, floor slabs, foundations, roof structure and roof cover) can be inferred from its BBR facade material, roof cover material and year of construction; where several catalogue solutions fit, one is drawn at random.
key_assumptions.supported_by: No validation against measured building data is reported; the procedure is described in Section 2.2 and the catalogue is supplied as supplementary information.

key_assumptions.assumption: Building dimensions can be derived from BBR attributes: height from the number of floors times a standard floor height, roof pitch from the roof cover material, perimeter from the footprint times a space-efficiency factor.
key_assumptions.supported_by: Stated as the dimensioning procedure; no empirical validation is reported.

key_assumptions.assumption: Dimensioning functions for internal walls estimated on the French building stock (Mailhac, 2019) transfer to the Danish building stock.
key_assumptions.supported_by: The authors state no Danish dimensioning studies exist and assume the two stocks are similar enough.

key_assumptions.assumption: Material amounts in foundations and ground-floor slabs are proportional to the building's footprint (uniform material quantities per m2 of footprint).
key_assumptions.supported_by: The authors concede that real amounts depend on location, soil conditions, height and building type, and cite Zimmermann et al. (2020) suggesting gross floor area would correlate better than footprint.

key_assumptions.assumption: The analysis sample is the set of BBR entries that survive pre-processing: entries with a missing year of construction, missing or unconventional roof/facade material, duplicates, negative floor area or floor count, and footprints or floor areas under 10 m2 are deleted (close to 16 % of entries, 12 % of reported gross floor area).
key_assumptions.supported_by: The authors state the exclusions make city-level material content 'probably underestimated' but improve estimates of typical material content per building type.

implies_edges.to: Estimated material amount in the building stock (kg)

key_assumptions.assumption: The BBR entries remaining after pre-processing are treated as correct.
key_assumptions.supported_by: The authors state explicitly that the cleaning does not guarantee the remaining data are correct.

threats_discussed: Foundations are modelled as generic material amounts per m2 of footprint and are named by the authors as one of the greatest sources of uncertainty and of difference between models
Basements, stairs, balconies and attics are not modelled separately in this first version of the model
Interdependences between macro-components (e.g. a floor slab incompatible with a given wall type) are not implemented
Non-residential buildings are largely not modelled separately although they are less standardised than residential ones
The cleaned BBR registry still contains entries with questionable values that pre-processing could not detect
Exclusion of close to 16 % of registry entries (12 % of gross floor area) means city-level material content is probably underestimated
robustness_checks: Comparison of the modelled material intensities with the archetype-level MICs of Lanau & Liu (2020) (Fig. 6)
Spatial visualisation of where the model gives lower or higher estimates than Lanau & Liu's model (Fig. A3)
Comparison of the modelled carbon replacement cost of Odense with Lanau et al. (2021)
No uncertainty analysis is carried out; the authors state that adding one would strengthen predictions
unresolved_confounders: The authors state the cleaned registry still had a significant number of entries with questionable values which could not be detected during preprocessing
The authors state the limited availability of measured data on the material content of buildings makes it difficult to compare the relative accuracy of the two models

identification.source_of_variation: None: no exogenous variation is used. The quantity is a deterministic bottom-up accounting estimate (or a direct tabulation) built from the administrative BBR building registry.

key_assumptions.assumption: Each building's macro-components (external and internal walls, floor slabs, foundations, roof structure and roof cover) can be inferred from its BBR facade material, roof cover material and year of construction; where several catalogue solutions fit, one is drawn at random.
key_assumptions.supported_by: No validation against measured building data is reported; the procedure is described in Section 2.2 and the catalogue is supplied as supplementary information.

key_assumptions.assumption: Building dimensions can be derived from BBR attributes: height from the number of floors times a standard floor height, roof pitch from the roof cover material, perimeter from the footprint times a space-efficiency factor.
key_assumptions.supported_by: Stated as the dimensioning procedure; no empirical validation is reported.

key_assumptions.assumption: Dimensioning functions for internal walls estimated on the French building stock (Mailhac, 2019) transfer to the Danish building stock.
key_assumptions.supported_by: The authors state no Danish dimensioning studies exist and assume the two stocks are similar enough.

key_assumptions.assumption: The analysis sample is the set of BBR entries that survive pre-processing: entries with a missing year of construction, missing or unconventional roof/facade material, duplicates, negative floor area or floor count, and footprints or floor areas under 10 m2 are deleted (close to 16 % of entries, 12 % of reported gross floor area).
